title: How a language model generates text: tokens, embeddings and context

videos.script: A model does one thing. Given some text, it scores every possible next piece of text. {{distribution}} Then something picks one piece, adds it to the text, and asks again. That loop writes every reply you have ever read from a model. {{loop}} In this lesson you put a model on your own computer first, and then watch that loop run on it. You install Ollama, download a model of three billion parameters, and build the small project every lesson works on. {{setup}} Then you ask the model for one step, and see the probabilities it gives the next token. You see text cut into tokens, which is what every price and every limit is counted in. {{tokens}} You turn sentences into vectors and see which ones land close together, and where that goes wrong. {{vectors}} And you see what a conversation really sends, because the model remembers nothing between requests. {{context}}
